units.translation: This particle has two meanings, one 'and', the other 'also', from which its manifold use can easily be derived, for the explanation of which sometimes several Latin words are needed. Wellauer collected and arranged the Aeschylean examples in a convenient order. It differs from τε, which is a connective particle, like the Latin -que.
καί [and] joins nouns
καί [and] joining pronouns
καί [and] joining adjectives or adjectives and participles
Especially frequent is πολὺς καί [much and] followed by another adjective, sometimes also an adverb.
καί [and] joining participles
καί [and] joining adverbs
καί [and] joining verbs
καί [and] joining periods and parts of periods
καί [also]
But
καί [also] placed after the word to which it refers.
καί [also] added to verbs with affirmative force.
καί [and indeed], and that.
καί [and] placed at the beginning of an interrogative sentence, continuing another person's speech
And without interrogation at the beginning of a sentence

A closer connection of members is effected by the particles τε and καί corresponding to each other, either with no word interposed or with one or more words interposed. In this way nouns are joined by τε — καί
τε - καὶ [both...and] joining pronouns
joining adjectives
joining participles
joining a participle with a finite verb
joining adverbs
joining verbs
joining parts of periods
τε καὶ – καί [both...and...and]
To words or sentences connected by καί, not rarely other things not necessarily connected with them are added by τε, which is a connective particle corresponding to Latin -que.

Examples of repeated καί differ in no way from the examples cited above where either two words or two parts of sentences are joined by καί, or where the same or different things are predicated of one thing.
From which is different
There is a triple καί
καί — δέ [and...but] correspond to each other
καί joined with other particles, and most often indeed καὶ γάρ or καὶ - γάρ, with one or more words interposed, so that it can be translated sometimes 'for also', sometimes 'for indeed'.
καὶ — γε [and...at least]. There are not a few examples of this among the passages indicated under the word γε on p. 66a.

καὶ δὲ [and but] with no word interposed the epic poets said, with one or more words interposed many other writers, but rarely the tragedians. We have cited Aeschylus' examples above on p. 78a, omitting
In the particles καὶ εἰ (by crasis κεί) καί is either a copula,
καὶ μάλα [and very]. See under μάλα || καὶ μὴν and καὶ μὴν γε see under μήν. || καὶ περ and joined καίπερ see under καίπερ. || καί and τοι coalesce into one word καίτοι, which see. || μὴ καί

καί by crasis coalesces with vowels and diphthongs, examples of which are indicated under the words with which καὶ coalesces. And first indeed with alpha privative, as κἀβδέλυκτα [and not to be loathed] fr. 130
